chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mukhtar, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Alawi, all together, from al-Fath ibn Yazeed al-Jurjani, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who killed his slave girl or his slave man, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the slave was owned by him, he would be disciplined and imprisoned, except if he is known for killing slaves, in which case he is killed for it.'

key_terms.فَيُقْتَلُ بِهِ: so he is killed for it

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a master who kills his slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a graduated legal framework for a master killing his slave, distinguishing between a one-time act requiring discipline and imprisonment versus habitual behavior warranting execution. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the master's character and pattern of behavior in determining the severity of the penalty, balancing retributive justice with the slave's status as property under specific conditions.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Al Mukhtar Bin Muhammad Bin Al Mukhtar, and Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Abdullah Bin Al Hassan Al Alawy, both together, from Al Fatah Bin Yazeed Al Jurjany,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who kills his slave girl or slave man. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was the owned slave of his, he would be disciplined and imprisoned, except if he happens to be well known with the killing of the slaves, so he would be killed due to it’.
